result.overall: The tribunal dismissed the refugee claims of the male claimant, his spouse, and their children from the Czech Republic, finding that the claimant did not establish a well-founded fear of persecution or lack of adequate state protection due to his Roma ethnicity.

themes.name: State protection adequacy
themes.summary: The tribunal extensively analyzed whether the Czech Republic provides adequate state protection to Roma individuals, concluding that the state has laws, agencies, and programs in place that are generally effective despite some local shortcomings.

themes.name: Claimant's efforts to seek protection
themes.summary: The claimant did not take all reasonable steps to seek state protection, including failing to follow up with police after reporting attacks, which undermined his claim.

themes.name: Country conditions and discrimination against Roma
themes.summary: The tribunal reviewed country conditions showing discrimination and violence against Roma but also government efforts to combat extremism and support Roma inclusion.

themes.name: Legal standards for refugee protection
themes.summary: The tribunal applied established legal principles requiring clear and convincing evidence to rebut the presumption of state protection in a functioning democracy like the Czech Republic.

arguments.quote: After the incident, the male claimant contacted the police and the police arrived at his house. The male claimant gave the police a physical description of the four skinheads that attacked him, his brother, and members of his family.
arguments.claim: The male claimant contacted the police after the skinhead attack at his home and gave a physical description of the attackers.

arguments.quote: The police did not follow up with the male claimant and did not provide him with any updated information concerning the findings of the investigation. The male claimant did not follow up with the police to find out if there were any developments with regard to the investigation of their case. I find that there is no persuasive evidence before me to show the police ignored the male claimant's complaint about the skinhead attack at his home. Nor do I find that there is any persuasive evidence to establish that the police did not conduct a proper and meaningful investigation into this criminal matter.
arguments.claim: The police did not follow up with the male claimant or provide updates on the investigation of the skinhead attack.
arguments.outcome_note: The police did not follow up, but there is no persuasive evidence they ignored the complaint or failed to investigate properly.

arguments.quote: The male claimant called the police after one of the windows in the house broke. The male claimant told the police what happened and explained that his children had been attacked by skinheads when they went to the downtown area of the city where they were living. In the opinion of the male claimant, the report he made to the police was useless because the police never did anything. The male claimant responded that that the police never followed up with him, nor did they approach him after he reported this incident to the police. I find that there is no persuasive evidence to show that the police, in this instance, did not conduct a proper investigation into the attack on his children and his home by skinheads ,or that they ignored the complaint made by the male claimant about these attacks.
arguments.claim: The male claimant reported the attacks on his children and the attack on his father-in-law's house to the police, but the police did not take effective action or follow up.
arguments.outcome_note: The police took notes and investigated, but the claimant did not follow up and there is no persuasive evidence of police neglect.

arguments.quote: As the male claimant was very frightened living in his house, he did not did make any efforts to get in touch with the police again. He said that he did not follow up because he was living in fear and he was afraid to let his children go outdoors and decided to stop sending his children to school. He said that because he and his family were so scared they did not follow up with the police.
arguments.claim: The male claimant was afraid to follow up with the police due to fear for his and his family's safety.

arguments.quote: Initially, the police blamed the male claimant for the fire in his building. The male claimant told the police that it had to have been skinheads who were behind the firebombing of their house. On the day of the fire, the police approached the male claimant and his family to talk about what had happened. The day following this incident, the police came to talk to the male claimant and his family.
arguments.claim: The police initially blamed the male claimant for the fire but later investigated the racial motive and spoke to the claimant and his family.

arguments.quote: The male claimant was asked if following the firebombing of his building the police had gone out in search of the perpetrators of this attack. The male claimant said that he did not know whether the police actually went searching for the perpetrators.
arguments.claim: The male claimant did not know if the police searched for the perpetrators of the firebombing.

arguments.quote: The police responded and arrived at the scene. However, it was too late; the skinheads had already fled the scene. The male claimant was asked if the police followed up with him after the attack at the train station. He said that they did not follow up. He said that because he and his family were so scared they did not follow up with the police.
arguments.claim: The police arrived after the train station attack but did not apprehend the attackers or follow up with the male claimant.
arguments.outcome_note: Police took notes and promised to inform the claimant but did not follow up; claimant did not pursue follow-up due to fear.

arguments.quote: Counsel for the claimant, in her oral submissions, indicated that in the past the Board has relied heavily on the June and July 2009 Issue Papers,37 but that more recent reports that post-date the Board's Issue Papers, especially a European Roma Rights Centre report covering January of 2008-April of 2011, an Amnesty International Report from March 16, 2011, and a news article from the Roma news dated August of 2011,38 rebut the findings of the earlier reports, indicating that the new laws, agencies and promises made by government officials in the Czech Republic are not "effective" in protecting the safety of the Roma community and improving their overall social and economic situation.
arguments.claim: The claimant's counsel argued that more recent reports post-dating the Board's Issue Papers rebut the earlier findings and show that new laws and government promises in the Czech Republic are not effective in protecting the Roma community.

arguments.quote: Counsel referred me to a recent Response to Information Request, number CZE103684.E, dated March 10, 2011.39 Counsel indicated that the information in this document establishes that the social inclusion program, which was referred to in the earlier Board's issue paper, was not "effective".
arguments.claim: Counsel referred to a March 10, 2011 Response to Information Request document to establish that the social inclusion program was not effective.

arguments.quote: Counsel also mentioned the reference in this document to the agency for social inclusion. Counsel said that this document establishes that the social inclusion program was ineffective.
arguments.claim: Counsel argued that the document establishes the social inclusion program was ineffective, citing the agency for social inclusion.

arguments.quote: During her oral submissions, counsel also referred me to another document which she argues demonstrates that efforts on the part of the Hungarian government to protect Roma are not effective. The headline of the report40 reads, "Czech Republic Police Fails to Protect the Roma of Novy Bydzov".
arguments.claim: Counsel referred to a report titled 'Czech Republic Police Fails to Protect the Roma of Novy Bydzov' to argue that Hungarian government efforts to protect Roma are ineffective.

holdings.quote: ANALYSIS Section 96 - Convention Refugee Grounds State Protection
holdings.statement: The analysis pertains to Section 96 regarding Convention Refugee Grounds and state protection.

holdings.quote: There is a presumption that a state is capable of protecting its citizens except in situations where the state is in a state of a complete breakdown.3 To rebut the presumption of state protection, a claimant must provide clear and convincing evidence of the state's inability to protect, absent an admission by the national's state of its inability to protect that national.4 While the effectiveness of the protection is a relevant consideration, the test is whether the protection offered is adequate.5 The evidence that state protection is not adequate must be reliable and probative and it must also satisfy me, on a balance of probabilities, that the state protection is inadequate.6 The claimant must approach the state for protection, providing that state protection might be reasonably forthcoming.7 In the absence of a compelling explanation, a failure to pursue state protection opportunities within the home state will usually be fatal to a refugee claim, at least where the state is a functioning democracy with a willingness and the apparatus necessary to provide a measure of protection to its citizens.8 Where a state is in effective control of its territory, has military, police and civil authority in place and makes serious efforts to protect its citizens, the mere fact it is not always successful at doing so will not rebut the presumption of state protection.9 A claimant cannot rebut the presumption of state protection in a functioning democracy by asserting only a subjective reluctance to engage the state.10 Doubting the effectiveness of the protection offered by the state when one has not really tested it does not rebut the existence of a presumption of state protection.11 The fact that state protection is not perfect12 does not constitute clear and convincing proof of the state's inability to protect its citizens, since no state can guarantee the protection of all its citizens at all times.
holdings.statement: There is a presumption that a state is capable of protecting its citizens except in situations where the state is in a state of a complete breakdown.

holdings.quote: Local failures to provide effective policing do not amount to a lack of state protection unless they are part of a broader pattern of the state's inability to provide protection.13 Indeed, if a claimant believes the actions of some police officers are corrupt, the onus is on them to approach other members of the security forces or authorities.14 There is nothing in the documentation before the Board to suggest that the Czech Republic is in a state of complete breakdown.
holdings.statement: Local failures to provide effective policing do not amount to a lack of state protection unless they are part of a broader pattern of the state's inability to provide protection.

holdings.quote: The Czech Republic generally respected and protected the rights of its citizens.
holdings.statement: The Czech Republic generally respects and protects the rights of its citizens.

holdings.quote: There is legislation in place that provides state protection for the Roma: including anti-discrimination and hate crime legislation.19 The Czech constitution prohibits discrimination based on national, racial or ethnic background as well as other pieces of legislation governing employment and education as well as The Charter of Rights and Freedoms.20 An anti-discrimination bill, which would harmonize Czech legislation with that of the European Union, was passed on June 17, 2009.
holdings.statement: There is legislation in place that provides state protection for the Roma, including anti-discrimination and hate crime legislation, and the Czech constitution prohibits discrimination based on national, racial or ethnic background.

holdings.quote: Furthermore, the Czech Republic is a member of the European Union, which has had a positive impact on the country by setting standards concerning human rights, as well as access to the European Court of Human Rights and access to multilateral programs such as The Decade of Roma Inclusion.21
holdings.statement: The Czech Republic is a member of the European Union, which positively impacts human rights standards and access to the European Court of Human Rights and multilateral programs such as The Decade of Roma Inclusion.

holdings.quote: The national police are responsible for enforcing the law and maintaining public order. Salary cuts at the Ministry of the Interior following government-wide fiscal austerity measures resulted in a lowered rate of retention among the national police force, especially among experienced detectives, which hampered the effectiveness of their work. Corruption remained a problem among law enforcement bodies.
holdings.statement: The national police are responsible for enforcing the law and maintaining public order, but salary cuts and corruption have hampered their effectiveness.

holdings.quote: The Ministry of the Interior oversees police actions and is responsible for investigating allegations of police misconduct. Observers believed that the ministry sometimes whitewashed wrongdoing or prematurely terminated investigations of units under its control.
holdings.statement: The Ministry of the Interior oversees police actions and investigates allegations of police misconduct, but sometimes whitewashes wrongdoing or prematurely terminates investigations.

holdings.quote: According to the Ministry of the Interior, police conducted 86 bribery investigations in 2010, handed over 37 cases of bribery for prosecution, twice as many as in 2009, and investigated 57 public officials for abuse of authority. In the first half of the year, records of the Ministry of Justice indicated that courts convicted 35 public officials of crimes relating to abuse of power, of which two were sentenced to prison, 24 were released on probation, and eight received fines. Of the 43 public officials convicted of bribery-related offenses, six were sentenced to prison, 27 were released on probation, and nine received fines.
holdings.statement: Police and courts have investigated and convicted public officials for bribery and abuse of authority, with several sentenced to prison or probation.

holdings.quote: Several ministries have anticorruption hotlines for citizens to report allegations. The Ministry of the Interior's anticorruption hotline, administered by the country branch of the NGO Transparency International (TI), received 4,653 calls in the first six months of the year. TI registered 400 new clients and identified 290 corruption complaints, 67 concerning the judiciary, 41 concerning police, 79 concerning property rights and construction permits, and 43 concerning public procurement.23
holdings.statement: Several ministries have anticorruption hotlines, including one administered by Transparency International, which received thousands of calls and identified numerous corruption complaints.

holdings.quote: The law mandates prison sentences of six months to three years for persons who deny Communist-era crimes or the Nazi Holocaust. Speech inciting hatred based on race, religion, class, nationality, or other group affiliation is also illegal and carries a sentence of up to three years in prison.
holdings.statement: The law mandates prison sentences for denying Communist-era crimes or the Nazi Holocaust and for speech inciting hatred based on race or other group affiliations.

holdings.quote: In June eight members of National Resistance, a neo-Nazi group, were indicted in Prague on charges of supporting and promoting Nazism. The individuals posted propaganda materials in public places and organized neo-Nazi events. The defendants each faced multiple counts with a possible total of eight years in prison if convicted.
holdings.statement: Neo-Nazi group members have been indicted and prosecuted for promoting Nazism and organizing events, facing possible prison sentences.

holdings.quote: Roma faced high levels of poverty, unemployment, and illiteracy as well as widespread discrimination in education, employment, and housing. Societal prejudice against the country's Romani population occasionally manifested itself in violence.
holdings.statement: Roma face high levels of poverty, unemployment, illiteracy, and widespread discrimination in education, employment, and housing, with societal prejudice sometimes manifesting in violence.

holdings.quote: Members and sympathizers of neo-Nazi organizations were the most frequent perpetrators of acts of interethnic violence, particularly against Roma. Ultranationalists were also active.
holdings.statement: Neo-Nazi organizations and ultranationalists are frequent perpetrators of interethnic violence against Roma.

holdings.quote: During the year neo-Nazi and skinhead rallies or marches took place in several cities. On March 14, a Molotov cocktail was thrown into a bedroom of a Romani home in the settlement of Bedrisk. Local police arrested a neighbor and her minor son on charges of attempted murder. On December 10, the regional court in Ostrava sentenced the boy to a three-year suspended sentence for attempted reckless endangerment and for his mother to an 18-month suspended sentence for not stopping her son from throwing the cocktail. On October 20, the court found all four guilty of attempted murder and property damage.
holdings.statement: Neo-Nazi and skinhead rallies and violent attacks against Roma homes have occurred, with some perpetrators arrested and sentenced, including for attempted murder and property damage.

holdings.quote: Vaculik, Mueller, and Lukes received 22-year sentence, and Cojocaru received a 20-year sentence. These are the longest sentences ever handed down for a racially motivated crime. The four were also required to pay seven million korunas ($389,000) for the child's medical expenses and a further 10.072 million korunas ($560,000) to the child and her family for pain and suffering.
holdings.statement: The longest sentences ever handed down for racially motivated crimes were given to perpetrators of a Molotov cocktail attack on a Romani family, including substantial financial compensation to victims.

holdings.quote: On November 27, Pavel Louda, mayor of Novy Bydzov, posted a statement on the city's official Web site declaring a "war on the gypsies." The prime minister and other government officials released statements condemning the mayor's actions. In December police opened an investigation of a young Czech man for promoting Nazism on Facebook. In May unknown persons attempted an arson attack against a Romani home in the village of Zdiby.
holdings.statement: Government officials condemned a mayor's statement threatening repressive measures against Roma, and police investigated promotion of Nazism on social media and attempted arson attacks against Romani homes.

holdings.quote: Over the previous two years, police focused greater attention on combating promoters of extremism. The Security Information Service (BIS), the country's civilian domestic intelligence agency, reported at the start of May that right wing extremist activity decreased in the country during the first six months of the year. BIS stated that developments involving neo-Nazis were particularly influenced by police raids in 2009 against members of extremist parties and the prohibition of the Worker's Party.
holdings.statement: Police have increased efforts to combat extremism, with reports indicating a decrease in right-wing extremist activity due to police raids and prohibition of extremist parties.

holdings.quote: In order to address acts of discrimination, the Czech Republic government introduced the Roma Police Assistants (RPAs).27 The purpose of employing RPAs is his to assist in building better relations and trust between the Roma and the police. The RPAs assist police in their investigations, assist in accompanying Romani who are victims of crime to file police reports and help obtain social services for such victims.
holdings.statement: The Czech Republic government introduced Roma Police Assistants to build better relations and trust between Roma and police, assisting in investigations and social services.

holdings.quote: It has been found that the RPAs and other minority liaison officers have been effective in helping the Roma. Furthermore, in the mid-1990s, the Ministry of the Interior (who is responsible for maintaining the national police force in the Czech Republic) initiated programs to combat extremism (including the neo-Nazis) by allowing the police to closely monitor such group activities and it is showing signs of success.28 The police have arrested neo-Nazis and they have been prosecuted, including a case where a Romani had been murdered. The police successfully prevented a clash of neo-Nazis in Brno and expelled them from the city.29 The government is also trying to recruit Roma as police officers, with the number of drives being conducted in Prague and Brno.
holdings.statement: Roma Police Assistants and minority liaison officers have been effective in helping the Roma, and police programs to combat extremism and recruit Roma officers show signs of success.

holdings.quote: If a Romani is interested in becoming a police officer but lacks the formal education requirement, the police offer assistance for that person to complete any education requirement so that they can then join the police force.30 Furthermore, the police are trained on how to deal with minorities.31 The police are making other efforts such as participating in day camps, seminars and school visits in order to foster better relations with the Roma.32 As of 2006, there were an estimated 61 Romani police officers in the Czech Republic.33
holdings.statement: Police offer educational assistance to Roma interested in becoming officers and are trained on how to deal with minorities, engaging in community activities to foster better relations.

holdings.quote: The judiciary has prosecuted hate crimes committed against the Roma on several occasions. The Issue Paper notes that judicial proceedings on racial crime have increased in recent years due to the efforts of NGOs. The Czech Ombudsman, created in 1999 and is known as the Public Defender of Human Rights, investigates allegations of public-sector mistreatment of Roma and takes corrective actions to remedy such situations.34 There are other government and non government agencies available to assist the Roma, including 400 Romani NGOs, the Czech Trade Inspectorate (to deal with unfair business practices or consumer discrimination), the Czech Helsinki Committee to investigate cases of police misconduct involving the Roma and the Social Inclusion Agency to ad in dress the social integration of the Roma into Czech society, including housing, healthcare, employment, social services and cohesion.35 The preponderance of the documentary evidence indicates that the Czech Republic government is making very serious efforts to provide protection to the Roma whether as victims of hate crime, assist in obtaining health care or education or inclusion into Czech society.
holdings.statement: The judiciary has prosecuted hate crimes against Roma, with increased proceedings due to NGO efforts, and the Czech Ombudsman investigates public-sector mistreatment of Roma and takes corrective actions.

holdings.quote: The Czech Ombudsman, created in 1999 and is known as the Public Defender of Human Rights, investigates allegations of public-sector mistreatment of Roma and takes corrective actions to remedy such situations.34 There are other government and non government agencies available to assist the Roma, including 400 Romani NGOs, the Czech Trade Inspectorate (to deal with unfair business practices or consumer discrimination), the Czech Helsinki Committee to investigate cases of police misconduct involving the Roma and the Social Inclusion Agency to ad in dress the social integration of the Roma into Czech society, including housing, healthcare, employment, social services and cohesion.35 The preponderance of the documentary evidence indicates that the Czech Republic government is making very serious efforts to provide protection to the Roma whether as victims of hate crime, assist in obtaining health care or education or inclusion into Czech society.
holdings.statement: There are numerous government and non-government agencies assisting Roma in areas such as housing, healthcare, employment, social services, and social integration.

holdings.quote: As noted above, there is discrimination against the Roma in various aspects of their lives. However the Czech government is making very serious efforts to overcome this discrimination.
holdings.statement: Despite ongoing discrimination against Roma in various aspects of life, the Czech government is making very serious efforts to overcome this discrimination.

holdings.quote: In this particular case, the male claimant was questioned as to what efforts he and his wife made to seek state protection before fleeing the Czech Republic.
holdings.statement: The male claimant and his wife made efforts to seek state protection before fleeing the Czech Republic.

holdings.quote: Between the year 2000 to 2003, the male claimant and his brother were attacked by skinheads at a restaurant. The skinheads were able to kick the door in and broke into the house. They then proceeded to beat the male claimant's wife and when the male claimant tried to defend his children the skinheads kicked them with army boots and beat them up.
holdings.statement: Between 2000 and 2003, the male claimant and his brother were attacked by skinheads at a restaurant and later at the claimant's house, where his wife and children were also beaten.

holdings.quote: I find that it is not reasonable to expect that the Hungarian police would be able to solve every criminal investigation involving an attack on a Roma family simply because they had a physical description of the perpetrators of the attack. There is no guarantee that a physical description of a perpetrator of a crime, without any other evidence, would guarantee a break in a criminal case leading to the identification, apprehension, and imprisonment of a criminal suspect. I find that even the best resourced, trained, and staffed police force in the world faces investigative challenges and obstacles which make it difficult to positively identify and apprehend criminal suspects. In this instance, the male claimant's description of the four skinheads to the police was that they were tall and all wore a uniform. Considering the limited information that the male claimant was able to provide to the Hungarian police concerning the identity of the perpetrators of the attack, I find that it is not surprising that the Hungarian police might be faced with a difficult task of trying to locate and apprehend the specific individuals who carried out the attack on him, his brother, and his family.
holdings.statement: It is not reasonable to expect the police to solve every criminal investigation based solely on a physical description of perpetrators without other evidence.

holdings.quote: During the time that the male claimant's children were living at the house of their grandfather, they experienced difficulties with their classmates and teachers at school. During the time the male claimant's children were living at their grandfather's house and were attending school, they had problems with skinheads. As they passed by the house, the skinheads threw rocks at the windows of the house and threatened the male claimant by saying that dirty gypsies should be gassed and that they were going to burn down his house. Some of the windows of the house were broken by the rocks that the skinheads were throwing.
holdings.statement: Between 2003 and 2004, the male claimant's children experienced harassment and attacks by skinheads at school and in the community, including attacks on their grandfather's house.

holdings.quote: In XXXXX of 2004, the male claimant and his family were subjected to a very frightening and potentially life-threatening ordeal. The male claimant and his family were able to get out of the building. Before they were able to exit the building, the male claimant noticed that the fire department and the police had already arrived on the scene. The fire department was able to put out the fire. They entered the building and removed 12 bottles of gas. The fire department was able to ascertain the cause of the fire. They determined that a gas bottle had been thrown onto the roof of the building, had broken one of the windows in the attic, and had dropped through the window onto a sofa which then subsequently ignited and caught fire.
holdings.statement: In 2004, the male claimant's house was firebombed by skinheads, and the police and fire department investigated the incident.

holdings.quote: Between 2004 and 2009, the male claimant continued to have problems with skinheads. In XXXXXXXX of 2004, the male claimant and his family were attacked by skinheads at a train station as they were getting ready to go and visit the male claimant's mother-in-law. When the male claimant's wife confronted the skinheads and asked them why they were calling her children names, the skinheads approached her and punched her with their fists. The skinheads then began to beat up everyone in the family. When the male claimant tried to defend the children, the skinheads beat him up also. The skinheads knocked out some of the male claimant's teeth.
holdings.statement: Between 2004 and 2009, the male claimant and his family continued to experience attacks by skinheads, including a violent attack at a train station.

holdings.quote: I find that there is no persuasive evidence before me to show the police ignored the male claimant's complaint about the skinhead attack at his home. Nor do I find that there is any persuasive evidence to establish that the police did not conduct a proper and meaningful investigation into this criminal matter. I find that there is no persuasive evidence to show that the police, in this instance, did not conduct a proper investigation into the attack on his children and his home by skinheads ,or that they ignored the complaint made by the male claimant about these attacks. I find that there is no persuasive evidence before me to establish that the police did not take the male claimant's complaint seriously or that they did not conduct a proper investigation into the attack perpetrated by skinheads against him and members of his family at the train station. However, there is no persuasive evidence to suggest that the male claimant followed up with their initial investigation to find out if there were any new developments or leads in the case, or if the police had been able to arrest or capture any of the perpetrators of the crime.
holdings.statement: There is no persuasive evidence that the police ignored the male claimant's complaints or failed to conduct proper investigations into the attacks by skinheads.

holdings.quote: I find that the male claimant, in the particular circumstances of this case, did not make diligent efforts nor did he take all reasonable steps in seeking out the assistance and protection of law enforcement authorities in the Czech Republic before coming to Canada in search of international protection.
holdings.statement: The male claimant did not make diligent efforts or take all reasonable steps to seek assistance and protection from law enforcement authorities before coming to Canada.

holdings.quote: Regarding the incident in 2000-2003 when the male claimant and his brother were attacked by skinheads at a restaurant and were subsequently attacked by the same skinheads at the male claimant's house along with members of his family, although the male claimant reported these incidents to the police, he did not follow up with them to find out the status of the ongoing investigation into this attack. Likewise, in 2003-2004, when the male claimant's children were attacked by skinheads in the downtown area of the city and the male claimant's house was subsequently attacked by skinheads marching past his house when they threw rocks at the windows of his house and broke one of those windows, although the claimant contacted the police for help and gave them a statement, he did not follow up with them to find out what if any progress was being made with regard to the investigation of his complaint. Finally, in XXXXXX of 2004, after the male claimant and his family were attacked by skinheads at a train station and the police showed up and took down a report of what happened, the male claimant once again made no efforts to follow up with the police about his complaint concerning this attack at the train station. I find that, despite the male claimant's fear and that of his family following the attack, it was the obligation of the male claimant to pursue his complaint with police authorities following the attack. However, he did not do so. I find that the male claimant's failure to follow up with the police is not objectively justified by the fact that he and members of his family were overcome by fear on account of the attack they had just sust
holdings.statement: The male claimant failed to follow up with police investigations after reporting attacks and incidents, which is not objectively justified by fear alone.

holdings.quote: According to this document, the government of the Czech Republic had in 2004, under pressure, implemented a number of laws and policies to address persistent systemic discrimination against the Roma. In this same document, it indicates that a senior research fellow at the Norwegian Institute of International Affairs (NUPI), writing in a November of 2010 publication for the Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS), questioned the effectiveness of those measures, "especially at the local level". I do not read this document as saying that all of the measures and policies adopted by the Czech government have been an abysmal failure and totally ineffective in addressing the persistent problem of discrimination against the Roma. What it actually says is that a senior fellow was calling into question the effectiveness of the measures; he does not definitively say that all the measures were completely "ineffective". Moreover, I find that what the senior fellow is saying is that he is calling into question the effectiveness of those measures especially at the local level; he is not saying that he is calling the effectiveness of these measures at a national level.
holdings.statement: The document shows that the Czech government implemented laws and policies in 2004 to address discrimination against the Roma, but a senior fellow questioned their effectiveness especially at the local level, not that all measures were completely ineffective.

holdings.quote: I find that this report is not demonstrative of a lack of state protection for members of the Romani minority in the Czech Republic. Additionally, I do not find that this report establishes that there is no effective protection available to members of the Roma community in the Czech Republic when faced with acts of extremism or racist violence.
holdings.statement: The report about the police failure in Novy Bydzov is not demonstrative of a lack of state protection for Roma in the Czech Republic and does not establish no effective protection is available against extremism or racist violence.

holdings.quote: I find that this report deals with a specific incident in a specific location at a specific point in time. According to Amnesty International, the police failed to protect three members of the Romani community from violent attacks by a group of far-right activists following a demonstration by a far-right Worker's Social Justice Party on March 12 in Novy Bydzov. I find that the case law is very clear that local failures in policing are not sufficient for the purposes of establishing a lack of state protection.
holdings.statement: The report deals with a specific incident at a specific time and place, and local failures in policing are insufficient to establish lack of state protection.

holdings.quote: I find that the male claimant, in the circumstances of this case, has failed to rebut the presumption of state protection with clear and convincing evidence.
holdings.statement: The male claimant has failed to rebut the presumption of state protection with clear and convincing evidence.

holdings.quote: Therefore, I am not persuaded that the Czech Republic would not be reasonably forthcoming with adequate state protection, should the claimant seek it.
holdings.statement: The Czech Republic would be reasonably forthcoming with adequate state protection if the claimant sought it.

holdings.quote: Therefore, I find the male claimant is not a Convention refugee and his claim under section 96 of the IRPA fails.
holdings.statement: The male claimant is not a Convention refugee and his claim under section 96 of the IRPA fails.

holdings.quote: The rest of the analysis of this decision will be under section 97 of the IRPA.
holdings.statement: The rest of the analysis of this decision will be under section 97 of the IRPA.

holdings.quote: For the same reasons articulated above, I find that the male claimant is not a person in need of protection.
holdings.statement: The male claimant is not a person in need of protection.

holdings.quote: Therefore, I find that the claim under section 97 of the IRPA fails.
holdings.statement: The claim under section 97 of the IRPA fails.

holdings.quote: As the claims of the spouse and the children are entirely dependent upon the claim of the male claimant, I find that their claims under section 96 and 97 of the Act also fail.
holdings.statement: The claims of the spouse and the children, being entirely dependent on the male claimant's claim, also fail under sections 96 and 97 of the Act.

holdings.quote: I determine that the claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
holdings.statement: The claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.

holdings.quote: The Refugee Protection Division therefore rejects their claims.
holdings.statement: The Refugee Protection Division rejects their claims.

rebuttals.quote: I disagree with counsel's interpretation of this document. I find that in order to properly interpret what is being said in this document, it must be read in the context of all the information presented in this document. I find that counsel is splitting hairs and has microscopically dissected this report.
rebuttals.court_answer: I disagree with counsel's interpretation of the March 10, 2011 document, finding that it must be read in context and that counsel has microscopically dissected the report.

rebuttals.quote: I disagree with counsel's interpretation. I find that when you read the contents of the document in the context of all the information in the report, what it is actually saying is that in one specific location, Brno, it became necessary for the agency to withdraw its services, because it could not effectively intervene in the inclusion process. However, the report goes on to say that the agency was going to continue its work in six out of the thirteen pilot locations until June of 2011.
rebuttals.court_answer: I disagree with counsel's interpretation that the social inclusion program was ineffective; the report states that in one location the agency withdrew services but continued work in other pilot locations.
